clue.text: Fairies manage to provide optical assistance

parts.note: peris are fairy-like beings of Persian myth, a crossword staple
to cope is to manage or get by

explanation.surface: Fairies somehow help someone to see better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A periscope is a tube of mirrors that lets an observer see over an obstacle: a visual aid.

clue.text: Counterfeit coin under control; note held

parts.note: P stands for a penny, a coin

indicators.note: held means the note is kept inside the phrase for under control

parts.note: in check means restrained, under control
B is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A forged coin is seized; a banknote is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: PINCHBECK is an alloy of copper and zinc imitating gold, hence sham.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck, the cheap alloy passed off as gold, came to mean sham or spurious.

clue.text: Italic type? Yes and no

parts.note: the ancient Italic peoples include the people of Rome, yet the upright typeface is the opposite of italic print

explanation.surface: Is it italic print or not?
explanation.definitionFit: Romans were an Italic people, but roman type is the upright face set against italics.

clue.text: Susan keeping Sir Patrick in uncertainty

indicators.note: keeping means holding the knight's surname inside the short name

parts.note: Sue is short for Susan
Sir Patrick Spens is the doomed sea captain of a Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: Susan holds on to Sir Patrick while unsure of what comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of anxious waiting for an outcome not yet known.

clue.text: One who watches over irregular verbs within

indicators.note: within puts the rearranged verbs inside the word over

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: irregular means out of the normal order, so the letters of verbs are mixed up

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher keeps an eye on irregular verbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' turns VERBS into BSERV, which goes inside OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is a watcher or onlooker.

clue.text: Your attention given first to what is unrefined

indicators.note: given first means the word for attention comes before the other piece

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Pay attention first to anything crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to what is' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy describes coarse, crude humour, lacking polish.

clue.text: No time to damage footwear

indicators.note: No says a word for time is dropped from the verb that follows

parts.note: to sabotage is to damage deliberately
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: With no time to spare, someone ruins a pair of shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time' looks like urgency; it tells you to remove AGE from SABOTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a type of shoe worn by peasants in France.

clue.text: Communication of note

explanation.surface: A message worth noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a message sent by sign; as an adjective it means remarkable, as in a signal success.

clue.text: Miss Everdene married David

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Thomas Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd
the wife of King David and mother of Solomon in the Bible

explanation.surface: Hardy's heroine weds a man named David.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy named his heroine Everdene after the Biblical woman whom King David took as wife.

clue.text: Dog-end — that's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for end wraps round the abbreviation for right

parts.note: the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt is roughly the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog-end' is British slang for a cigarette butt; split it into 'Dog' and 'end'. 'that's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow and track them.

clue.text: Avenger is after retreating Londoners, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the word is behind the reversed piece
retreating means going backwards, so the word for the Londoners is read in reverse

parts.note: SE MEN, men of the South East of England, of whom Londoners are an example

explanation.surface: Some avenging figure pursues Londoners as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns SEMEN (SE men, South-East men) into NEMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so she is an avenging spirit.

clue.text: Racing about with a gun, lots of soldiers

parts.note: re means about or concerning
gat is old slang for a pistol
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone goes around with a gun among many troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races, so the word stands for racing on water.

clue.text: The turning-point of the match, in general

indicators.note: of says the answer is a part drawn out of the words that follow, as letters spanning them

explanation.surface: Commentators pick out the decisive moment of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across matcH IN GEneral; 'in' here is part of the run, not a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the pivot on which a door turns, and figuratively the point on which something depends.

clue.text: Man in the back with girl, getting practice

indicators.note: in places the word for the man inside the word for the back

parts.note: the rear is the back
he is a male person
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A man sits at the back with a girl and they get some practice in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run before a performance.

clue.text: With some relief, managed to follow me back

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for managed after the reversed piece
back means the little word me is read the other way round

parts.note: bossed means directed or managed

explanation.surface: Someone was in charge and, with some relief, came after me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With some relief' sounds like a sigh but means raised in relief, as a pattern on metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An embossed design is raised from the surface, that is, carved or stamped in relief.

clue.text: Guard one starting game, accepting pay rise

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the reversed pay goes inside the person

parts.note: a beater drives game birds out of cover for the guns

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word for pay goes backwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A guard who starts a match demands a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns FEE into EEF. Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders guarding the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Beefeater is one of the Yeoman Warders who keep watch at the Tower of London.

clue.text: Hold the fort

definitions.meaning: to retain or retain possession of
a castle's main tower, its last stronghold

explanation.surface: An order to defend a position.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep is to hold on to something; a keep is the strongest tower of a castle, its central stronghold.

clue.text: Initially passionate meeting of boy and girl could result in it

definitions.text: Initially passionate meeting of boy and girl could result in it

indicators.note: Initially takes just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: Reg is a boy's name, short for Reginald
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A passionate first date between a lad and a lass might lead to a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting of' and 'and' join the pieces, and the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Conception after lovemaking leads to expecting a baby.

clue.text: Winter days frozen up, without one bit of fire

indicators.note: without means leaving out the letter for one
up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ice is frozen water
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ember is a glowing fragment of a fire

explanation.surface: Winter days freeze over with no fire to warm them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ICE into ECI; 'without one' drops the I, leaving EC.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth month falls in winter in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Scratch, having a tie

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a beard
a draw is a tied result

explanation.surface: A competitor pulls out because of a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch a horse or player is to pull it out of a race or contest.

clue.text: Sharp, a note within the range

indicators.note: within puts the note inside the word for range

parts.note: ken means range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A piercing sound, one note within the instrument's range.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen describes a cutting edge, so it is a synonym of sharp.

clue.text: Think about arranging time and date

indicators.note: arranging tells you to put the letters of the two words in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ponders how to fix an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect deeply, ponder or contemplate.

clue.text: Exclusive group in a club, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is said like the word for the club

parts.note: a cleek is an old Scottish iron golf club

explanation.surface: A select set of members within a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The club is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small closed circle of people who shut others out.

clue.text: Divide tinned order

indicators.note: order here means put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A command to split up canned goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To indent is to notch or cut apart, as indentures were split along a toothed line.

clue.text: Mercenary general, retired into the country

indicators.note: into puts the reversed general inside the country

parts.note: France is the country

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the general's name is read backwards

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general of the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A soldier of fortune, once a general, goes off to live in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns LEE into EEL, which goes inside FRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A free lance was originally a medieval knight who sold his services to any lord, a hired soldier.

clue.text: Money for composer without a royalty

indicators.note: without means the letter for royalty is dropped

parts.note: César Franck was a Belgian-French composer
K is the abbreviation for king, a royal

explanation.surface: Money for a songwriter who gets no royalties.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and remains that of Switzerland.

clue.text: Being subject to error

definitions.meaning: fallible, as in to err is ...

explanation.surface: Being prone to make mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a being, and people are fallible: to err is the mortal condition.

clue.text: End up with a cry of pain, a beastly cry

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Ending up crying out in pain, like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIM into MIA. 'with a' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call is the classic animal noise.

clue.text: Against what, to the French, is dated

parts.note: anti means opposed to
que is French for what

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to what the French regard as old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is old, belonging to an earlier era.

clue.text: Compact, non-profit-making organization does

definitions.meaning: a charity rules out gain, read as two words

explanation.surface: A tidy little charity is busy at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is a deal agreed between parties; and a charity forbids itself profit, which read as two words is bar gain.

clue.text: Dog that's a Nobel prize-winner

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dog that has won a Nobel prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Curie won Nobel prizes in physics and chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie and Pierre Curie both won Nobel prizes for their research on radioactivity.

clue.text: Fail to take advantage of a war. Why? To order!

indicators.note: to order means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bewildered question about why a war was started and missed its chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'To order!' is the anagram signal, taking in 'To' as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste an opportunity is to squander or discard it.
